summary: This article explains how families across Arabia burn fragrant wood chips called bakhoor, blended with precious resins like oud, to scent their homes and welcome guests.
introduce: Start a K-W-L chart on the board and ask students what they already Know and what they Want to know about the topic of “Bakhoor and Incense: Scents of Arabia”. Tell them they will fill in what they Learned after reading.

keyTerms.def: a rare, costly resin from a special tree, used to make scents
a mixture of different things combined together

challengeTerms.def: a sticky substance that comes from certain trees or plants
a skilled worker who makes things carefully, often by hand

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that old traditions like burning bakhoor matter less now that modern air fresheners exist? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why bakhoor is an important part of hospitality in Arabia.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review oud, fragrance, and blend, and let weak readers use a K-W-L chart and read the article with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use aromatic, resin, and artisan in a short paragraph that connects the article to something they learned in another subject.
